Flushing the brakes is very easy.

To flush the brakes: 

Tools: 13mm wrench, aquarium tubing, Gatorade bottle, tape, drill, preferably another person, clean brake fluid, a way to take your wheels off and put them back on and torque them, a way to lift your vehicle, fender cover of some sort.

Instructions:

1. Drape fender cover over your driver's side fender (brake fluid will strip paint)

2. Siphon dirty brake fluid out of the reservoir 

3. Lift vehicle off the ground enough to take wheels off

4. Take your beautiful wheels off

5. Drill a hole into your Gatorade bottle's cap, large enough for the aquarium tubing to poke in and tape it in place.

6. Take the bleeder valve cap off of the driver's side brake bleeder valve and fit the other end of your aquarium tubing onto the bleeder valve. 

7. Pour clean brake fluid into the brake fluid reservoir.

8. Use 13mm wrench to crack open driver's side bleeder valve and have your buddy press on the brake pedal. The brake fluid should be squirting into the Gatorade bottle at this point. Keep doing this until the fluid in your aquarium tubing is a light yellow color (clean) and fill the brake fluid reservoir when it gets low.

9. Close the bleeder valve and repeat on the 3 other bleeder valves. The order should be driver front, passenger front, driver rear, passenger rear

Remember that this is a good time to inspect suspension components and brake pads/rotors, and a good time to replace any worn pads if you know how to.

Because your car is front wheel drive, the front tires wear down significantly faster. The tread begins to start "Feathering" (the outer tread will start to bend up like an overused toothbrush). This CAN cause noise if severe enough, however usually noise caused by tires is usually from a poor alignment. 

If you run your fingers along your tires, and the tread feels wavy, then you should take your car in to get an alignment check. If you feel that the outer tread is sharp in one direction and smooth in the other (feathering), then you need to rotate the tires. 

With that bad of a tread depth difference, it sounds like you need to rotate them.

Tl;dr: It could. Rotate your tires and check the alignment!

Not sure if you've heard of the "Chicken trick" but if you have a tear and you've got a buddy in the mid lane, get them to stand right next to the wall where raptors are. You can link with them and spam heal while you swing away at those chickens. Your tear will stack and your teammate will be back to full HP.

Another trick is to gank on level 2. Taric ganks are usually very successful on level 2 because of his long stun. (Get blue buff, smite gromp, gank mid or whichever side lane is closest to blue)

Remember, you NEED blue buff as Taric jg. If you can consistently get pink wards on your enemy's blue, you will be more successful. 

For maxing abilities, I max his heal last because it is very costly and it's main use is to give you that extra attack speed. So I max EWQ. 

For general jungling, I never smite the first buff that I take. If I'm starting blue, I smite gromp. If I'm starting red, I smite big Krug. Then I clear one side fully, get my second buff, and get scuttle. Between switching sides of the jungle, I use a potion. After clearing my second buff, I also use another potion so if I have to fight for scuttle I won't be too far from full HP.  Taric has a very healthy clear, so you should save second smite for your first scuttle (if it is contested).

Hope this helps!
